name: Strazik House
notes: From the east approach views down the vine path (a long closed bar of pigmented board-marked concrete, one recess in the middle with a local-stone wall and the glazed entrance, a slit window to the north, two young poplars at the entrance), the dusk aerial (the bar on a low stone-edged platform, gravel forecourt with low gabion walls), the west view over the vines (roof slab running out over a glazed living gallery at the north end, a concrete fireplace block standing out on the terrace, two flues, pool with a small spa in lawn and paving, bedrooms along the south part glazed between concrete piers) and the corner view (big end window, raised stone planter). Orientation from the article: circulation spine to the east, every room open west to the Andes; the pool end placed north from the camera positions. Length (~48 m) scaled from the aerial against a ~4 m wall; depth, bay widths and pool size estimated. The vineyard is shown as a few rows of vines running east-west, the way the path runs. The cellar is inside and not shown. Dark steel frame of the bedroom entry niche omitted; the planter terrace sits on the south end by guess. Refinement pass (24 Sep 2026): the living gallery under the roof slab was 6.7 m deep, so in the isometric views the slab hid its glass completely; it is now a 1.7 m recess under a slab 0.4 m proud, which reads as a dark glazed band in shade under the roof edge, as in the west view. The fireplace block now stands at the slab edge with its dark firebox door, and the second flue sits over it. The bedroom bays on the west are recessed 1.2 m, not 0.4, so the concrete piers between them read. The two young poplars at the entrance are real poplars now (the new tree shape), with two more at the ends of the east forecourt from the corner view. The entry niche on the east face is lined in its dark steel frame (drawn in the renderer's dark, which is greyer than the real brown). The spa moved off the pool's south end, as in the west view. Still guessed: the depth of the gallery, the exact bay widths, the second pair of poplars, and the vine-row direction on the west side. Refined 24 Sep 2026 (three rounds against the west view 04, the aerial 02 and the approach views 00/13): the vines were thin 1.2 m walls 3 m apart, reading as fences; they are now 0.9 m-wide, 1.4 m-high canopies every 2.5 m, the dense rows of the photographs; the living gallery's glass now wraps round the north end of the bar under the roof slab, as photo 04 shows the corner open, with a dark room behind it so it reads.
